question: Does the retained reversal characteristic shape remain photographically useful and severe-safe when execution is intrinsically RGB-cube-preserving rather than post-hoc Lab gamut compressed?

operator.compiled_curve: exact CB7 three-channel mean normalized-transmittance PCHIP; no refit
operator.application: apply the same scalar curve independently to each linear RGB channel, then blend y=(1-strength)*x+strength*curve(x)
operator.cube_contract: curve maps 0 to 0 and 1 to 1; blend is convex; no clipping or gamut compression
operator.jacobian_contract: diagonal derivative is at least 1-strength and all off-diagonal entries are zero

controls.joint_basic: per-image joint EV/WB/contrast/saturation fit on the exact sample from source to candidate
controls.source_boundary: new epsilon boundary relative to source
controls.gradient: linear-RGB p99.9 gradient magnitude and adjacent material L-star sign inversion

stop_rules: Do not change curve, strength, channel domain, source population, basic control or gates after candidate pixels are scored.
Any automatic or confirmed severe-artifact failure closes this exact channelwise compiler without strength, colour-space, curve, source or threshold rescue.

Pass may retain a generic film-inspired colour-tone mechanism for a fresh direct comparison with fixed AO6; it cannot establish Velvia calibration, scene exposure, dye colour, authenticity, preference or product promotion.
claim_ceiling: Rights-cleared photographic development evidence for an intrinsically cube-preserving generic RGB operator compiled from a retained first-party reversal characteristic shape; not Velvia calibration, stock colour, scene exposure, authenticity, preference or product promotion.
